home.title: FOUND: Foundation Data for Industrial Tech Transfer
home.tagline: Bridging Academic Progress and Practical Impact through Domain-Grounded Data
home.subtitle: ECCV 2026 Workshop

overview.mission: Foundation models have pushed computer vision forward, but their reliability often drops in real-world, domain-specific deployments due to long-tail distributions, domain shift, and operational constraints (privacy, safety, cost). Closing this "last-mile" gap requires not only better models, but domain-tailored datasets that capture rare yet critical corner cases and realistic variability. Building on the first FOUND workshop, we refer to this missing piece as Foundation Data: fine-grained, domain-grounded data designed to bridge academic progress and practical impact. FOUND is organized around two coupled pillars — Foundation Data creation and practical tech transfer — with a key focus on Physical AI and World Models.
keyTopics: Foundation Data creation: collection from non-Internet domains, curation and labeling at scale, self-/semi-/weak supervision, and synthetic/simulation data
Practical tech transfer: adaptation, robustness to OOD/long-tail conditions, and deployment/evaluation protocols aligned with operating reality
Physical AI and World Models: data and transfer strategies for embodied, interactive settings
Temporal and multimodal streams, sim-to-real transfer, and safety-aware evaluation
Continual adaptation and domain-specific deployment protocols

core: Foundation Data creation: collection, curation, and labeling for non-Internet and domain-specific settings
Self-supervised, semi-supervised, and weakly-supervised learning for domain-grounded data
Synthetic and simulation data for bridging domain gaps and covering rare corner cases

formatNotice.title: About this format
formatNotice.intro: Unlike a standard peer-reviewed CFP, this workshop uses a self-nomination and curatorial invitation format. Please note:

points.label: Open curation, not blind review.
points.text: Nominations are reviewed openly by the organizing committee for topical fit, potential to spark discussion, and overall balance of the poster session. Selected presenters are invited by email; there is no scored peer review.

points.label: In-person poster presentation.
points.text: Selected work is presented at the workshop's poster session, with at least one presenter attending ECCV 2026 in person.

points.label: No proceedings, limited online exposure.
points.text: Invitations do not come with any official publication or Springer proceedings. Only presentation titles and presenter names appear on this website; abstracts and posters stay within the workshop audience.

formatNotice.closing: You are therefore welcome to nominate work that has already been accepted elsewhere, as well as work in progress that you would prefer to keep in a closed setting.

nominationGuidelines: Nominations are submitted via the Google Form linked below
Provide a presentation title, a short abstract (~200 words), and presenter name and affiliation
Optionally include a link to a related paper, preprint, project page, or code repository
Anonymization is not required — nominations are reviewed openly by the organizers
Work at any stage is welcome: published, in submission, or in progress
Nominators must register for and attend ECCV 2026 in person to present their poster

faq.question: Can I nominate work that has already been published?
faq.answer: Yes. Nominations may include published, unpublished, or work in progress, as long as it aligns with the workshop's topics of interest.

faq.question: What information should I include in the nomination?
faq.answer: A presentation title, a short abstract (~200 words), presenter name and affiliation, and optionally a link to a related paper, preprint, or project page.

faq.question: How are nominations selected?
faq.answer: Selections are made by the organizing committee based on topical fit and the overall balance of the poster session. There is no scored peer review.

faq.question: Do I need to attend the workshop in person if invited?
faq.answer: Yes. Invited presenters are expected to attend and present their poster in person during the workshop.
